A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LOT Merging. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite formatting changes and additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision and vision-language experiments, including performance comparisons, parameter ablations, exemplar sensitivity, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original language-model evaluations, generalization tests, corruption studies, and feature-drift analyses.

M1.justification: The layer-wise objective, closed-form merging rules for linear weights, scaling factors and biases, and final lambda-weighted integration remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 corrects a comment without changing its operations; the additional backbones use the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds eight GLUE language tasks and MTEB retrieval and clustering tasks, extending evaluation beyond vision and vision-language. It also adds unseen-task and corrupted-input scenarios and uses AOKVQA and IconQA as auxiliary exemplar sources alongside existing datasets.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds the Individual fine-tuned BLIP models as a reference comparator, absent from that comparison in v1. Comparator membership in the retained vision experiments is unchanged; the new appendix evaluations primarily reuse existing comparison methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include merging six experts and evaluating two held-out tasks, Gaussian-blurred or surrogate exemplars, seven corruptions applied to exemplars and test data, and restricted exemplar-class coverage. Language evaluations introduce RoBERTa and Qwen3-0.6B settings with classification, correlation, retrieval and clustering metrics. These are added designs, not demonstrated changes to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendices D.8, D.9, D.11 and D.12 add substantial analyses of unseen-task transfer, calibration-data mismatch, corruption robustness, multimodal feature-drift correlations, and incomplete exemplar-class coverage. v1's existing parameter ablations, exemplar sensitivity, runtime and consistency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: D.11 and Table 17 add explicit Pearson correlation estimates between feature drift and loss changes across six BLIP tasks, extending the earlier visual association analysis. Three-random-exemplar averaging and the runs in Table 8 remain unchanged; no new confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing LOT results, including 82.7% for ViT-B/32 and 90.5% for ViT-L/14, are retained. v2 adds Individual BLIP scores and Tables 11–18, including a GLUE average of 63.13 and Qwen ArguAna performance of 47.36 versus Task Arithmetic's 30.86. These are additional results under new settings, not improvements over v1 under matched conditions.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects expert-side activations from f_k^(-1)(W_k) to f_k^(l-1)(W_k) in Equations 22–23 and subsequent steps, repairing the recursive proof's layer indexing. The feature-drift bound, assumptions, and closed-form derivations are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: training-free feature-drift minimization, closed-form layer-wise merging, task-dependency analysis, and the reported 4.4-percentage-point ViT-B/32 advantage. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these main claims.

C2.justification: D.8 adds qualifications about narrower advantages on unseen tasks and task-dependent benefits from surrogate exemplars. D.11 interprets differing multimodal correlations through reasoning demands and modality interactions. The original limitations concerning strictly data-free use and more complex operations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit source-code link and clarifies that exemplars are randomly drawn from training data and kept separate from evaluation data. It also identifies the Qwen checkpoints used in the new experiments. The split statement is newly disclosed information, not evidence of a changed split; existing hardware and implementation disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for RoBERTa, GLUE, MTEB and Qwen3 to support the language experiments. The related-work discussion and positioning against RegMean, Surgery and CAT Merging remain substantively unchanged; conversion to numbered citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: The core exposition and section order are largely retained. Changes include updated author and affiliation text, expanded acknowledgments, corrected equation references and an algorithm comment, a NeurIPS checklist, and additional appendix subsections rather than extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: Tables 11–18 substantially expand the displayed evidence with generalization, corruption, language-model, correlation and exemplar-coverage results. Table 3 gains a reference row, and the NeurIPS format reflows existing material and resizes Figure 2. Figures 1–3 retain their underlying analyses.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical support by testing language models and directly examining calibration representativeness, unseen-task transfer and corruption sensitivity, which v1 left untested. The Individual BLIP reference and clearer exemplar provenance also improve assessability. Localized reporting errors temper this gain: Table 11 reports 51.1 for an unseen-task average whose entries average 48.6, and D.8 claims surrogate-exemplar superiority despite OKVQA scoring 40.15 versus Task Arithmetic's 40.37. These errors warrant correction but do not outweigh the substantial expansion of relevant evidence.
